note: Nested-package findings from parity/express/nested/sanitizehtml/. Both were found by running sanitize-html@2.17.6 and the port over the same inputs and comparing; both are fixed in the working tree but unfixed in every published version, so the advisories are drafts until a release goes out.

findings.summary: sanitizehtml performs no URL scheme validation on any attribute, so javascript: and data: URLs survive in href, src and every other URL-bearing attribute the caller allows
findings.description: ## Summary `sanitizehtml.Sanitize` does not validate URL schemes at all. Upstream `sanitize-html` filters every URL-bearing attribute against `allowedSchemes` (`http, https, ftp, mailto, tel`) and drops the attribute when the scheme is not permitted. The port keeps the attribute verbatim, so a `javascript:` or `data:text/html` URL passes straight through into the sanitized output. This is broader than an earlier draft of this finding stated. That draft claimed `href`, `src` and `cite` were scheme-checked and only the other sixteen attributes were missed. Direct execution against the published module disproves that: `href` is not checked either. ## Verified against the published module Reproduced against `github.com/malcolmston/express@v0.4.0`, the latest published version: ```go opts := sanitizehtml.Options{ AllowedTags: []string{"a"}, AllowedAttributes: map[string][]string{"a": {"href"}}, } sanitizehtml.Sanitize(`click`, opts) // => click (payload retained) // Same for every other URL attribute, e.g.: //
